item: ITEM 4: the Cadence-profile double-click grow (LMB double-click, `xschem select_grow_connected [x y]`) must also select the wire labels on the wires it selects, so that Delete after it removes the connected material. Overrules decision O2 (rings are wires only) of /home/analog/dev/xschem-claude/doc/claude/specs/dblclick_connected_select.md for wire labels. All five code and spec files involved are unmodified in the working tree relative to d36cb429e (git status --short printed nothing for them).
mechanism:
READ IN CODE (nothing below was run).

Gesture path: Tk `<Double-Button-1>` on a design canvas runs `xschem callback %W -3 %x %y 0 %b 0 %s` (binding text quoted in tests/headless/test_calc_pick.tcl; installed by set_bindings in src/xschem.tcl) -> callback() -> handle_double_click() in src/callback.c. For Button1 under `cadence_compat`, when ui_state is 0 or SELECTION, or a transient arm is live (`STARTWIRE` with `pin_pending`, or `STARTMOVE|STARTCOPY` with `!mouse_moved`), it: calls abort_operation(1) and zeroes drag_elements if transient; restores `dblgrow_level = dblgrow_level_save`; sets `dblgrow_last_press_was_grow = 1`; calls select_grow_connected_step(mousex, mousey, 1); sets `place_click_committed = 1`; returns. Otherwise (stock profile) it falls to edit_property(0) or the draw-gesture termination code.

select_grow_connected_step() in src/select.c, pick_seed arm: find_closest_obj(mx,my,1) names the seed (empty space: return, nothing logged); seed id is wire[].id or inst[].id, else 0; a different (type,id) zeroes dblgrow_level; level++ capped at 3; then RECOMPUTE: unselect_all(1), select_object(mx,my,SELECTED,1,NULL) under select_at_suppress_log, dblgrow_apply_level(level). Coordless arm: compares lastsel with dblgrow_sel_sig (a selection COUNT), zeroes the level on a mismatch, level++, then dblgrow_apply_level(level>=3 ? 3 : 1) on the live selection. Tail (both arms): rebuild_selected_array(); `dblgrow_sel_sig = lastsel`; one log_action line (`xschem select_grow_connected %.10g %.10g` with snap_to_grid coords, or the bare verb); draw_selection if has_x; returns the level. It pushes no undo.

dblgrow_apply_level(): level<3 calls grow_one_ring_wires() `level` times; level>=3 loops `while(grow_one_ring_wires() > 0)`.

grow_one_ring_wires() ("one ring"): hash_wires(); hash_instances(); rebuild_selected_array(); then walks the sel_array snapshot (select_wire only sets need_reb_sel_arr, so wires added in this call are not expanded: exactly one ring). WIRE entry: init_wire_iterator over the wire's ordered bbox (wire_spatial_table buckets), and for each unselected wire k the four-way endpoint-on-span test (touch() of each endpoint of one against the span of the other, exact doubles, the same test as check_connected_nets and the netlister's wirecheck). ELEMENT entry: for every PINLAYER pin, get_inst_pin_coord -> get_square -> wire_spatial_table[sqx][sqy] -> touch(wire k, pin). Marks with select_wire(k, SELECTED, 3, 1) (quiet, nodraw, override_lock). Returns the number of WIRES added. No instance is ever selected: that is the whole of O2, and why a label stays unselected and survives the Delete.

check_connected_nets(stop_at_junction, n) (static, src/select.c): (1) INSTANCE loop, always run: init_inst_iterator over wire n's bbox (inst_spatial_table, instances hashed by their bbox in hash_inst), type test `type && (IS_LABEL_SH_OR_PIN(type) || !strcmp(type,"probe"))`, requires `sym->rect[PINLAYER]` non-NULL, reads PIN 0 ONLY with get_inst_pin_coord(k,0), `touch(wire n, x0, y0)` -> sets `inst[k].sel = SELECTED` directly (no select_element, no lock test) and need_reb_sel_arr. (2) WIRE loop only when `!(stop_at_junction & 2)`: touching wires get `.sel = SELECTED` and the function RECURSES. So check_connected_nets(2, w) is exactly 'select the label/pin/probe instances whose pin 0 touches wire w', with no wire growth and no recursion. IS_LABEL_SH_OR_PIN (src/xschem.h) = label, ipin, opin, scope, show_label, iopin, bus_tap; so the one-shot's set is those seven plus probe. No device type is in it. It reads `(inst[k].ptr + sym)->type` with no `ptr < 0` guard.

select_connected_nets(stop_at_junction): for each selected WIRE calls check_connected_nets; for each selected ELEMENT, per pin: wires touching the pin are selected and passed to check_connected_nets, and instances in the same bucket whose type is exactly `label` or `probe` (and not skip_instance) with a pin at the SAME coordinate are selected.

What 'a label is on a wire' means elsewhere in the product (all read): netlister name_attached_nets()/wirecheck()/name_attached_inst_to_net() in src/netlist.c use touch(wire, pin) anywhere along the span, and exact coordinate equality pin-to-pin; label_ride_capture() and fluid_label_on_copper() in src/move.c use inst_is_netlabel(i) (type exactly `label`, src/check.c, exported in xschem.h), `rects[PINLAYER] >= 1`, pin 0, touch() against every NON-degenerate wire; point_on_wire_or_pin() in src/check.c is the Add-Wire-Label drop gate (on any wire span, endpoints included, or exactly on an instance pin). With `label_splits_wires` 0 (default, src/xschem.tcl) a type=label pin does not split a wire, so a lab_wire sits in the interior of one xWire. `wire_label_vjust` is not a symbol in src/: it is only the name of doc/claude/wire_label_vjust_batch/ (issues 1623 to 1625, by file name, about vertically justified label text).

Symbols with type=label (grep of the K/G blocks): xschem_library/devices/lab_pin.sym, lab_wire.sym, lab_generic.sym, bus_connect.sym, vdd.sym (global=true), gnd.sym (global=ground); 27 files under xschem_library/gschem_import (power and port shapes), 3 under xschem_simulator, 3 under sky130A/xschem_libs, 1 under ihp-sg13g2 (sub.sym, carries global=). type=show_label: lab_show.sym, bus_connect_nolab.sym. Ports: ipin.sym, opin.sym, iopin.sym. type=probe: spice_probe.sym and five others. type=bus_tap: bus_tap.sym (two pins). `global` is read instance prop first, then symbol prop (netlist.c name-nodes code; pin_rename_is_global_name() in src/editprop.c is the two-step precedent).

Candidate scopes and their exact tests: (a) labels only, power symbols included: `inst_is_netlabel(i)`; (a-minus) labels without power symbols: `inst_is_netlabel(i)` and the `global` token (instance, then symbol) is neither `ground` nor boolean true; (b) labels plus schematic ports: `type && IS_LABEL_OR_PIN(type)`; (c) everything the one-shot takes: `type && (IS_LABEL_SH_OR_PIN(type) || !strcmp(type,"probe"))`. Each also needs `inst[i].ptr >= 0` and `rects[PINLAYER] >= 1` before get_inst_pin_coord(i,0).

Readers of the grow's result: handle_button_release() (snapshots dblgrow_level into dblgrow_level_save and zeroes it on any Button1 release whose press was not the -3 grow; consumes place_click_committed at its top and forces mouse_moved=1, which is what suppresses the cadence 'deselect everything but the object under the cursor' collapse on release 2); handle_button_press() (clears dblgrow_last_press_was_grow on every Button1 press); dblgrow_sel_sig (a count, type-agnostic); the log line (no level, no object list); delete() in src/select.c (one push_undo, inst_delete_compact of every selected instance, delete_wires(SELECTED), then maintain_wire_segments() under autotrim_wires); edit_property() in src/editprop.c (`set_first_sel(0,-2,0)` returns the first ELEMENT of sel_array when the stored first_sel is not a still-selected ELEMENT, so with a wire seed and labels selected `q` targets a label, where today it targets the wire); label_ride_capture() (a label that is itself selected is never ridden: it gets LEASH mode under connect_by_kissing or is placed by the plain ELEMENT commit; wire_label_ride.md 16.4 names ALT-R/ALT-F as the gesture where that differs); slickprop::on_selection_changed at release.

design_options.name: A. Labels as leaves: one label pass after the rings
design_options.sketch: Leave grow_one_ring_wires and the wire walk alone. Add a static helper in src/select.c that, for every instance passing the chosen scope test (inst_is_netlabel for scope a) with ptr >= 0 and rects[PINLAYER] >= 1 and not yet selected, reads pin 0 with get_inst_pin_coord and selects it with select_element(i, SELECTED, 3, 1) when touch() holds against any SELECTED, non-degenerate wire. Call it once in select_grow_connected_step's shared tail, after dblgrow_apply_level and BEFORE rebuild_selected_array / `dblgrow_sel_sig = lastsel`. So that a label the grow added is not an expansion source on the next coordless step, the ELEMENT arm of grow_one_ring_wires skips a net-label instance whose pin already touches a selected wire (a label seed with no selected wire under it still expands, which keeps row T3). Result: the WIRE set at every level is identical to today's; labels at level N are those touching a wire selected at rings up to N; the whole-net level takes every label touching the flooded copper; labels joined only by NAME and labels on a pure X crossing do not carry the grow.
design_options.risks: The ELEMENT-arm skip is a new rule that needs its own row (a label on a pure crossing, both forms). A full instance scan per step is O(instances x selected wires); the instance bucket iterator is the cheaper spelling but relies on a label's bbox containing its pin (what check_connected_nets already relies on). Selected labels change what `q` targets and how ALT-R/ALT-F treats them (see traps).
design_options.blast_radius: src/select.c only for the engine (one helper, one call, one guard in the ELEMENT arm). No change to callback.c logic, scheduler.c logic, log format, escalation state or undo. Comments in select.c, scheduler.c, callback.c, cadence_style_rc; the spec; two suites.

design_options.name: B. Labels interleaved per ring (labels become expansion sources)
design_options.sketch: Select labels inside each ring pass and let the existing ELEMENT arm expand from them on the next ring; make the level-3 loop continue while wires OR labels were added.
design_options.risks: Changes the wire set in one geometry: a label on the interior of two wires that cross without a junction carries the grow to the crossing wire. The netlister does give both wires the label's name, so it is defensible, but it departs from 'rings are geometric wire adjacency' and from today's wire rows. The fixpoint condition must count labels or the whole-net level stops one pass early and the coordless form then disagrees with the coordinate form. Ring count per level becomes harder to state.
design_options.blast_radius: grow_one_ring_wires and dblgrow_apply_level both change; every wire-count row in the suite has to be re-derived on fixtures with labels.

design_options.name: C. Reuse check_connected_nets(2, w) for each selected wire
design_options.sketch: After the rings, call the existing static function with bit 2 for every selected wire: it marks instances whose pin 0 touches the wire and does not grow wires.
design_options.risks: Its type set is scope (c) only: ports (ipin, opin, iopin), scope, show_label, bus_tap and probe come in, so a Delete after the grow removes schematic ports (the cell's interface) and probes. It writes inst[].sel directly (no lock test), reads the symbol type with no unbound-symbol guard (the issue 0498 shape), tests `rect[PINLAYER]` non-NULL rather than a count, and does not skip degenerate wires. Narrowing it means adding a parameter to a function the Shift-RMB and Ctrl-RMB gestures share.
design_options.blast_radius: Smallest diff if scope (c) is what the user wants; otherwise it touches the older one-shot's core.

design_options.name: D. Replace the ring engine with select_connected_nets
design_options.sketch: Use the one-shot for the rings.
design_options.risks: Not workable as rings: with bit 2 a selected wire gains no wire at all, without it the function recurses to the whole net in one call. It also draws and rebuilds on its own.
design_options.blast_radius: Rejected; listed because the spec's 'Reused infrastructure' section still suggests it.

recommended: Option A with scope (a): symbols whose type is exactly `label` (inst_is_netlabel), which takes lab_pin, lab_wire, lab_generic, bus_connect and the vdd/gnd power symbols, pending the user's answer on power symbols and ports. Reasons from the code: the predicate already exists and is the one the label ride, the splitter and the weld barrier use for 'a net label'; the wire walk stays byte-for-byte what the 42 existing rows measure, so every existing wire row is a regression fence for free; the label pass is a pure function of the selected wire set, so the recompute-from-seed property (selection at level N is a function of seed and N) holds; nothing in callback.c, the log line, the escalation state or undo has to move. Level semantics to write into the spec: level N selects the wires of rings up to N plus every label whose pin touches one of them; level 3 selects every label touching the flooded copper; a label seed stays selected and the wires touching its pin are ring 1 (unchanged); a device is never added; labels that share only a NAME with the net are not reached (rings stay geometric, the name-wise chord is Ctrl+Alt+Shift+LMB).
